tagline: Across Ohio on the first coast-to-coast road for cars.
intro: The Lincoln Highway comes into Ohio at East Liverpool on the Ohio River, a town whose pottery industry was once the largest in the country, and crosses the northern part of the state for 241 miles by way of Lisbon, Canton, Wooster, Mansfield, Bucyrus and Lima to Van Wert. Ten county courthouses stand along the way. The mapped roads follow older alignments as well as US 30, so they add up to a good deal more than 241 miles.

It was dedicated in 1913, one of the first highways laid out expressly for automobiles, and ran from Times Square to San Francisco. In Ohio one section followed an ancient Indian trail known as the Ridge Road.

moments.title: Cindell and Baywood Streets
moments.text: Just east of Canton two stretches of brick laid for the original highway survive, a rare thing anywhere along its 3,389 miles.

moments.title: Crestline
moments.text: Two Lincoln Highway pillars stand at the corners of Clink Boulevard, one for J. F. McMahon, the town's first highway consul, and one for Austin F. Bement of the Lincoln Highway Association.

moments.title: Gomer
moments.text: In October 1939 Admiral Byrd's Antarctic Snow Cruiser, bound from Chicago to Boston, went off a small bridge here into a stream, and in three days 125,000 people came to see it.
